questions.question: Why must the two vectors in $x\cdot y$ have matching coordinate positions?

Because the result must have the same dimension as $x$
Because each coordinate of $x$ is paired with the corresponding coordinate of $y$
Because the last coordinate is always ignored
questions.explanation: $x\cdot y=\sum_i x_iy_i$ multiplies each coordinate of $x$ with the CORRESPONDING coordinate of $y$, so they must align.

option_explanations: It multiplies ALL corresponding coordinates, not only the first.

No coordinate is ignored; every position contributes.

questions.question: When can $x\cdot x$ be equal to $0$ for a real vector $x$?

Whenever the coordinates of $x$ add to $0$
questions.explanation: $x\cdot x=\sum_i x_i^2$ is a sum of squares, which is $0$ only when every $x_i=0$, i.e. $x=\boldsymbol0$.

questions.question: The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality bounds $|x\cdot y|$ above by:
